title: Balanced Binary Tree
statement: Given a binary tree as a level-order list `root`, return `true` if it is height-balanced: for every node, the heights of the left and right subtrees differ by at most 1.

predict_steps.prompt: At the left child 2, the left chain goes 3→4 while the right child is missing. About how tall is the left side vs right?
Does that make the whole tree balanced?
predict_steps.hint: Any node with height gap > 1 fails the check.

viva.question: How can you detect height-balance in one linear DFS?
expected_points: each node returns a height or a failure sentinel
a node is balanced only when both children are balanced and their heights differ by at most one
failure bubbles upward without finishing useless work
every node is still visited at most once on success

viva.question: Is a single-node tree balanced?
expected_points: yes, there is no skew between children
the absolute difference is zero which is allowed
the base case returns a valid height instead of failure

viva.question: Why abort early when a subtree returns unbalanced?
expected_points: the whole tree fails as soon as one subtree fails
further height arithmetic cannot repair that failure
propagating the sentinel avoids extra recursion
balance is a global property that requires every subtree to pass
